title: Topic: dolo 650 hepatotoxicity side effects
description:
But remember that high doses of it inhibit PDXK(*), the enzyme that converts pyridoxine to P5P.   

This leads to the buildup of inactive pyridoxine which is in fact neurotoxic, particularly to sensory neurons.   

(*) Pyridoxine is converted to pyridoxal 5'-phosphate through phosphorylation (it is phosphorylated by the enzyme pyridoxal kinase (PDXK) to pyridoxine-5'-phosphate (PNP) a process that needs zinc and Mg) and oxidation (via pyridoxine-5'-phosphate oxidase, requiring riboflavin/FMN so it needs B2) to the active P5P.

title: Topic: dolo 650 hepatotoxicity side effects
description:
How to kill fatty liver ! 

NASH.
NAFLD.
Fatty Liver Disease.

New terminology:
• MASLD replaces NAFLD
• MASH replaces NASH

Why was the name changed?

Because the disease is mainly driven by:
• Insulin resistance
• Obesity
• Metabolic syndrome
• Diabetes
• High triglycerides

So the focus shifted from “non-alcoholic” to the real root cause: metabolic dysfunction.

Different names for the same metabolic fire.

What begins as “just a little fat in the liver” can slowly progress to inflammation, insulin resistance, fibrosis, cirrhosis, and finally liver failure.

The dangerous part?
Most people feel “normal” for years.

Fatty liver is often treated like a minor ultrasound finding.
In reality, it is one of the earliest visible signs of metabolic dysfunction.

It is strongly linked with:
• Central obesity
• Type 2 diabetes
• High triglycerides
• Hypertension
• PCOS
• Sleep apnea
• Cardiovascular disease
• Chronic inflammation

The liver is not getting sick alone.
The entire metabolic system is under stress.

Common clues:
• Large waistline
• Excess abdominal fat
• Constant fatigue
• Post-meal sleepiness
• Indigestion and bloating
• Skin darkening around neck, underarms, groin or eyelids (acanthosis nigricans: a marker of insulin resistance)

Investigations:
• LFT (ALT, AST, GGT)
• Fasting insulin and HOMA-IR
• Lipid profile
• Ultrasound abdomen
• FibroScan for fibrosis staging

Now the most important part:

The treatment is not hidden.
Human physiology already knows the answer.

The liver heals best when insulin levels fall consistently.

That is why these habits work powerfully:

• Early dinner
• Avoid late-night eating
• Walking after meals
• Sleeping with an empty stomach
• Morning exercise in fasting state
• Resistance training + running
• Adequate hydration and electrolytes
• Reducing ultra-processed foods and sugar

During fasting periods:
Water, electrolytes, lemon water, or black coffee may help some individuals tolerate fasting better.

Why does this work?

Because fatty liver is largely a disease of chronic caloric excess, continuous insulin stimulation, physical inactivity, poor sleep, and loss of metabolic flexibility.

For most of human history, people naturally had:
• Longer fasting windows
• More physical movement
• Less processed food
• Better circadian alignment

Modern humans eat all day and move very little.
The liver stores the consequence.

A healthy liver is not built inside a pharmacy.
It is built in daily routine, meal timing, movement, sleep, and discipline.

The body still remembers the old biology.
We just stopped living according to it.

@DocPriyamMD All of them can be damaged by alcohol. ✅

A) Brain → cognitive impairment, peripheral neuropathy, cerebellar degeneration, Wernicke–Korsakoff syndrome

B) Liver → fatty liver, alcoholic hepatitis, cirrhosis

C) Heart → alcoholic cardiomyopathy, arrhythmias (“holiday heart syndrome”), hypertension

D) Pancreas → acute and chronic pancreatitis

So the correct answer is:

A, B, C, and D
